Methods for zinbreg objects

Source: R/methods-zinbreg.R
zinbreg-methods.Rd

Standard S3 methods for fitted zero-inflated negative binomial regressions returned by zinbreg().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.zinbreg'
print(
  x,
  digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L),
  signif.stars = getOption("show.signif.stars"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
coef(object, model = c("full", "count", "zero"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
vcov(object, model = c("full", "count", "zero"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
residuals(object, type = c("pearson", "response"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
predict(
  object,
  newdata,
  type = c("response", "count", "zero", "prob"),
  at = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

...

Further arguments (currently unused).

object, x

An object of class "zinbreg" (or "summary.zinbreg" for the print method of the summary).

signif.stars

Logical; show significance stars?

model

For coef() and vcov(): "full" (count and zero coefficients, named count_* and zero_* as in pscl::zeroinfl()), "count" or "zero".

type

For residuals(): "pearson" (default) or "response". For predict(): "response" (marginal mean \((1-\pi)\mu\)), "count" (NB mean \(\mu\)), "zero" (structural-zero probability \(\pi\)) or "prob" (matrix of \(P(Y = k)\) for k in at).

newdata

Optional data frame in which to look for covariates.

at

For type = "prob": the counts at which to evaluate the probabilities (default 0:max(y)).

Value

coef() a named vector; vcov() a matrix; logLik() an object of class "logLik" with df = number of count and zero coefficients

  • 1 (for \(\theta\)); fitted(), residuals() and predict() numeric vectors (a matrix for type = "prob"); nobs() the number of observations with positive weight; summary() an object of class "summary.zinbreg" with coefficient tables for both model parts.

Examples

data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")
fit <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + kid5 + ment | ment, data = bioChemists)
coef(fit, model = "zero")
#> (Intercept)        ment 
#>  -0.7949062  -0.6193810 
AIC(fit)
#> [1] 3123.505
nd <- data.frame(fem = "Men", kid5 = 0, ment = c(0, 10, 40))
predict(fit, newdata = nd, type = "response")
#>        1        2        3 
#> 1.128592 2.088116 4.339573 
predict(fit, newdata = nd, type = "zero")
#>            1            2            3 
#> 3.111162e-01 9.213804e-04 7.852850e-12 
# expected number of zeros
sum(predict(fit, type = "prob", at = 0))
#> [1] 286.3748
